messages.content: 計算加熱100克水從攝氏25度到攝氏100度所需的能量（單位為焦耳），並計算在相同條件下加熱相同質量的鋁所需的能量（單位為焦耳）。

function.name: temperature_converter_convert
function.description: Convert a temperature from one unit to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

temperature.description: The temperature to convert. This is a float type value.

round_to.description: The number of decimal places to round the result to. Defaults to 2.

function.name: energy_calculator_calculate
function.description: Calculate the energy needed to heat a substance from an initial to a final temperature. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in grams. This is a float type value.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the substance in degrees Celsius. This is a float type value.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the substance in degrees Celsius. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit to report the energy in. Options are 'joules' and 'calories'. Defaults to 'joules'.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to calculate the energy needed to heat 100g of water from 25°C to 100°C, unit joules. Also calculate energy needed to heat same mass of aluminum under same conditions, unit joules.

We need to use the function energy_calculator_calculate. Provide substance, mass, initial_temperature, final_temperature, unit='joules'.

We need to call twice: once for water, once for aluminum.

We should output the results. Probably we can do two calls or combine? The function expects a single call with parameters. We can call twice.

We need to produce JSON calls to the function. According to guidelines, we should not provide additional text besides the function call. But we can provide multiple calls? Usually we can only call one function at a time. But we can chain calls: first call for water, then after receiving result, call for aluminum. But we can also combine into one call? The function signature doesn't allow multiple substances. So we need two calls.

Thus we will first call energy_calculator_calculate for water. Then after receiving result, call again for aluminum.

We need to include the function name and arguments. We'll do:

{
"name": "energy_calculator_calculate",
"arguments": {
"substance": "water",
"mass": 100,
"initial_temperature": 25,
"final_temperature": 100,
"unit": "joules"
}
}

Then after receiving result, call again with substance "aluminum".

We should not add extra text. We'll just output the function call JSON.
